page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.2xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance built on KVM virtualization architecture. Powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz, this x86_64 instance provides 4 physical cores and 8 vCPUs. It features 64.0 GB of system memory, delivering a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The CPU instruction set includes AVX, AVX-512, AES, BMI2, ADX, and FMA, supported by 33 MB of L3 cache. Local storage is omitted, requiring network-attached storage configurations, and network connectivity is provided at a baseline rate of 2 Gbps. The instance contains no GPU acceleration hardware.

Performance testing highlights a high-RAM configuration designed primarily for memory capacity rather than raw compute throughput. Single-core and multi-core CPU benchmarks reflect lower-tier compute scores, including a Geekbench multi-core result of 3552. However, uncached memory bandwidth demonstrates solid stability at 39.75 GB/sec for reads and 36.51 GB/sec for writes. The server handles key-value store operations effectively, reaching 5.94 million Redis SET operations per second. The primary trade-off is modest CPU compute performance in exchange for dense memory allocation per vCPU. Ideal workloads include Redis or Memcached caching tiers, small-to-medium database servers, and memory-bound background tasks.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.2xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud instance configured with 8 vCPUs across 4 physical Intel Xeon 8163 cores at 2.5 GHz and 64.0 GB of RAM. Operating on a KVM hypervisor with x86_64 architecture, it delivers 8.0 GB of memory per vCPU and includes support for AVX-512 and AES instructions. The server features no local SSD storage and provides a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth without discrete GPUs. Benchmark evaluations show weak single-core and multi-core CPU metrics, balanced by moderate uncached memory bandwidth of 39.75 GB/sec read and solid Redis throughput of 5.94 million SET operations per second. The hardware trade-off favors high memory density over raw compute speed, positioning this server as a cost-effective solution for memory-intensive workloads, in-memory key-value caching, and database applications that do not demand heavy parallel CPU processing.
